name: Typography
controls: The typeface class and letterform treatment of every word on screen, how type is laid out in the frame, and how it moves.
question: What kind of lettering should carry the words?
notes: Main options are visual type classes and surface treatments; they stack (a condensed grotesk can be outlined and extruded). A common professional pairing is one class for display and one for text (e.g. high-contrast serif headlines over a neo-grotesk UI face), which is why pick.max is 2. Classification terms are not standardized: 'grotesk', 'neo-grotesk' and 'neutral sans' are used loosely in tech branding, and many contemporary faces are hybrids (Space Grotesk is a grotesk reworked from a monospace; Inter is a neo-grotesk tuned for screens). 'Liquid', 'chrome', 'inflated' and 'distorted' type are studio and trend terms, not formal classifications. Commercial typefaces named here are references only; HyperFrames renders web fonts, so prompts name a Google Fonts face first and treat commercial names as the target look. Composition and motion are facets because any class can be laid out or animated any way; SplitText (free since GSAP 3.13) splits into chars, words or lines for the motion facet.

options.what: A low-personality sans designed to disappear behind content, typically a screen-tuned neo-grotesk.
options.looks: Even color, large x-height, moderate apertures, no quirks; tight negative tracking at display sizes. Google Fonts: Inter, Geist, IBM Plex Sans, Roboto. Commercial: SF Pro (Apple), Helvetica Now, Söhne.
options.motion: Unobtrusive line-by-line or word-by-word masked reveals, crisp scale on UI labels, rolling numbers.
options.use: SaaS launch films, UI-led explainers, captions, product labels, data callouts.
options.conveys: Clarity, competence, product-first; the brand speaks through the interface, not the letters.
options.vs: Neutral sans is a role, not a historical class: it is usually a neo-grotesk. A grotesk has visible irregularity; a geometric sans shows circles and straight lines. 'Neutral' is informal usage.
options.prompt: Set all type in Inter (or Geist): headlines weight 600 at 96-140px on 1080p with letter-spacing -0.03em and line-height 1.0; body and labels weight 400-500 at 28-36px with 0 tracking. One family only, sentence case, no decorative treatments; hierarchy comes from size and weight, never color alone.

options.what: The first sans serif genre (19th to early 20th century): slightly irregular stroke contrast, quirky details and a less systematized rhythm.
options.looks: Uneven widths between letters, visible stroke contrast, spurred G, often double-story g, tight apertures, a faintly handmade warmth. Google Fonts: Space Grotesk, Schibsted Grotesk, Familjen Grotesk, Bricolage Grotesque. Commercial: Akzidenz-Grotesk, Franklin Gothic, Söhne, GT America.
options.motion: Punchy word-by-word cuts, big tight-tracked headlines that scale or slide as blocks, kinetic layout reflows.
options.use: Tech and design-tool brands with an editorial edge, agency reels, fashion-tech, creative tools.
options.conveys: Confident, contemporary, a little raw; designed but not corporate.
options.vs: Neo-grotesk (Helvetica, Univers) rationalizes the grotesk into uniform widths and horizontal terminals; grotesk keeps the quirks. Geometric sans is built from circles and lines instead. Contemporary marketing uses 'grotesk' loosely for any sans with character.
refs: Söhne by Klim Type Foundry (used by OpenAI)
options.prompt: Set headlines in Space Grotesk or Bricolage Grotesque weight 600-700 at 120-200px on 1080p, letter-spacing -0.04em, line-height 0.92, left aligned; let the typeface's irregular widths show at large size. Pair with a quieter neo-grotesk (Inter 400) for small text. Keep color flat, one accent at most.

options.what: The mid-century rationalized grotesk: uniform widths, horizontal terminals and closed apertures, built for systematic, grid-driven design.
options.looks: Dense, even texture, near-monolinear strokes, very regular rhythm, strong at heavy weights. Google Fonts: Inter, Hanken Grotesk, Archivo, Instrument Sans. Commercial: Helvetica / Neue Haas Grotesk, Univers, Neue Montreal.
options.motion: Swiss-style grid motion: text blocks snap along columns, masked line reveals, tracking compression on arrival.
options.use: Corporate and product films, Swiss-grid layouts, museum and cultural identities, wayfinding-style info graphics.
options.vs: Grotesk is its older, quirkier ancestor; neutral sans is the role it usually plays in UI; geometric sans draws O as a true circle while a neo-grotesk O is a squarish oval.
options.prompt: Set type in Inter Tight or Archivo, weights 500 and 800 only, aligned flush-left to a 12-column grid with 80px margins on 1920x1080. Headlines 140-180px, letter-spacing -0.035em, line-height 0.95; supporting text 28px. Objective, no italics, no ornament; red or black as the single accent.

options.what: A sans constructed from near-perfect circles, straight lines and triangles, with minimal stroke contrast.
options.looks: Round O, single-story a (often), pointed or flat apexes, wide round bowls, open airy counters. Google Fonts: Jost, Outfit, Poppins, Manrope, Sora, Urbanist. Commercial: Futura, Avenir (geometric-humanist), Circular, GT Walsheim, Brandon Grotesque.
options.motion: Smooth scale and position tweens, letter morphing (round glyphs morph cleanly), friendly pop-ins with gentle overshoot.
options.use: Consumer apps, fintech, startup brands, onboarding and explainer films.
options.conveys: Friendly modernity, approachability, optimism; rounder faces read as consumer, sharper ones as Bauhaus.
options.vs: A neo-grotesk draws a squarish oval O and a double-story a; a geometric sans uses a circle and usually a single-story a. Rounded sans softens terminals; geometric sans is about construction, not corner softness.
options.prompt: Set type in Outfit or Manrope: headlines weight 600 at 110-160px on 1080p, letter-spacing -0.02em, line-height 1.05; body weight 400 at 30px. Emphasize round glyphs (o, a, e) at display size. Pair with generous spacing and rounded UI shapes; no condensed widths.

options.what: A sans whose proportions and stroke modulation follow calligraphy and classical roman letters, with open apertures.
options.looks: Open c, e and a, subtle stroke modulation, varied letter widths, often a true italic; highly legible at small sizes. Google Fonts: Open Sans, Source Sans 3, Fira Sans, Nunito Sans, Lato (semi-humanist). Commercial: Gill Sans, Frutiger, Myriad, FF Meta.
options.motion: Calm line-by-line reveals, readable subtitles, gentle tracking, soft fades with small translation.
options.use: Healthcare, education, government and public-service explainers, long captions, accessible products.
options.vs: Neo-grotesks close their apertures and even out widths; humanist faces keep them open and calligraphic. Geometric sans ignores the pen entirely.
options.prompt: Set type in Source Sans 3 or Fira Sans: headlines weight 600 at 90-120px on 1080p with 0 to -0.01em tracking and line-height 1.1; body weight 400 at 32px, line-height 1.4. Use sentence case and a real italic for emphasis. Reveal text line-by-line so it can be read comfortably.

options.what: A text-derived serif of moderate contrast used at display sizes for a magazine or book voice.
options.looks: Bracketed serifs, moderate contrast, elegant italics used for emphasis words; often set large with tight leading. Google Fonts: Instrument Serif, Newsreader, Fraunces, Source Serif 4, EB Garamond. Commercial: Tiempos, GT Sectra, Canela, Lyon.
options.motion: Slow masked line reveals, italic word swaps, cross-fades, restrained drift; rarely bouncy.
options.use: Premium product launches, AI and research brands, editorial explainers, brand manifestos.
options.vs: High-contrast serif (Didone) has hairline thins and vertical stress and reads as fashion; editorial serif is softer and more literary. Slab serifs have unbracketed block serifs and low contrast.
options.prompt: Set headlines in Instrument Serif or Newsreader at 120-180px on 1080p, weight 400, letter-spacing -0.02em, line-height 1.0, with one emphasis word in italic. Pair with a neo-grotesk (Inter 400-500, 26-30px) for labels. Reveal lines with a bottom-up mask over 700-900ms, ease power3.out.

options.what: A serif with extreme thick/thin stroke contrast, vertical stress and hairline, often unbracketed, serifs.
options.looks: Razor-thin hairlines, heavy verticals, ball terminals, dramatic at large sizes and fragile at small. Google Fonts: Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, Bodoni Moda, Abril Fatface. Commercial: Didot, Bodoni, Canela Deck, GT Super.
options.motion: Slow scale drift, long masked reveals, elegant tracking expansion, hard cuts on a beat; hairlines need slow motion to stay visible.
options.use: Fashion, beauty, luxury, perfume, hospitality and premium consumer launches.
options.vs: Editorial serif is lower contrast and literary. 'Modern' here is a historical term (late 18th century Didot/Bodoni), not a synonym for contemporary.
options.prompt: Set display type in Bodoni Moda or Playfair Display at 160-260px on 1080p, weight 400-500, letter-spacing -0.01em, never below 48px so hairlines survive video compression. Pair with a small, widely tracked (0.2em) uppercase sans at 20-24px. Move it slowly: 1.2-2s scale drift from 1.04 to 1.0, ease power2.out.

options.what: A serif with thick, block-like, usually unbracketed serifs and low stroke contrast.
options.looks: Sturdy, typewriter-adjacent, heavy blocky serifs, strong horizontal emphasis. Google Fonts: Roboto Slab, Zilla Slab, Arvo, Bitter. Commercial: Rockwell, Clarendon, Archer, Sentinel.
options.motion: Weighty stamps and slams, scale punch with a hard landing, poster-like cuts.
options.use: Editorial explainers, craft and food brands, Western or industrial themes, newsroom graphics.
options.vs: Editorial serifs have bracketed, tapered serifs and contrast; monospace faces often have slabs but fixed widths.
options.prompt: Set headlines in Zilla Slab or Roboto Slab weight 700 at 120-160px on 1080p, letter-spacing -0.01em, line-height 1.0. Land them as solid blocks: scale 1.15 to 1.0 in 250ms, ease power4.out, no bounce. Pair with a plain sans for supporting text.

options.what: A typeface in which every glyph occupies the same horizontal advance.
options.looks: Grid-like columns, wide i and l, slashed or dotted zero, code and terminal associations. Google Fonts: JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, Space Mono, DM Mono, Geist Mono. Commercial: Berkeley Mono, Söhne Mono, GT America Mono.
options.motion: Typewriter, scramble/decode, cursor blink, character-by-character reveals; fixed widths prevent layout jitter while characters change.
options.use: Developer tools, AI and infra launches, terminal demos, data labels, technical captions.
options.conveys: Technical credibility, precision, hacker culture, machine voice.
options.vs: Pixel type is built on a bitmap grid; monospace is only fixed in width. Tabular figures in a proportional font also align numbers without making the whole face monospace.
options.prompt: Set technical text and labels in JetBrains Mono or IBM Plex Mono weight 400-500 at 24-40px on 1080p, uppercase labels tracked 0.08em; use it for code, numbers and captions while headlines use a sans. Animate by character: typewriter at 35-50ms per character with a 530ms blinking block cursor, or scramble/decode.

options.what: Typefaces designed only for large sizes, where personality outranks readability.
options.looks: Exaggerated proportions, ultra weights, unusual construction, idiosyncratic details. Google Fonts: Syne, Unbounded, Anton, Dela Gothic One, Rubik Mono One. Commercial: Druk, GT Maru Mega, Ogg.
options.motion: Big kinetic moves: scale punch, full-frame word slams, stretch and squash, type as transition.
options.use: Title cards, brand stings, event promos, social-first ads, music visuals.
options.conveys: Loudness, personality, energy; the type is the image.
options.vs: Display is a use class that overlaps condensed, extended and treatment options; any class set huge is not automatically display type.
options.prompt: Set a single statement in Syne ExtraBold or Unbounded Black at 220-400px on 1080p, filling 70-90% of frame width, letter-spacing -0.04em, line-height 0.85. Maximum 4 words per screen. Everything else is tiny (20-24px). Cut between statements on the beat rather than fading.

options.what: Letterforms that imitate pen, brush or marker writing; script faces connect letters, hand faces often do not.
options.looks: Irregular baselines, varied stroke weight, loops and ligatures. Google Fonts: Caveat, Kalam, Permanent Marker (marker), Dancing Script, Great Vibes (formal script). Commercial: Brush Script, custom lettering.
options.motion: Write-on (stroke draw-on along the letter path), handwritten annotations appearing over UI, slight wobble.
options.use: Annotations and callouts, personal or community brands, education, food, lifestyle.
options.conveys: Humanity, informality, personal touch; formal scripts convey ceremony.
options.vs: Hand lettering is custom drawn; handwritten fonts repeat identical glyphs, which looks fake when a letter recurs large. Scripts join letters; casual hands do not.
options.prompt: Use Caveat or Kalam weight 500-700 only for annotations and short asides (max 5 words), 40-64px on 1080p, rotated -2 to -4 degrees, paired with drawn arrows. Reveal it as write-on: convert to SVG paths and animate stroke-dashoffset from path length to 0 over 600-900ms, ease none, then fill.

options.what: A narrow-width style that fits more characters per line and allows very tall headlines.
options.looks: Tall, tight columns of letters, often heavy and uppercase, poster and sports energy. Google Fonts: Anton, Bebas Neue, Oswald, Barlow Condensed, Big Shoulders Display. Commercial: Druk Condensed, Tungsten, Knockout, Trade Gothic Condensed.
options.motion: Vertical masked reveals, fast stacked-line slams, horizontal stretch from compressed to regular width.
options.use: Sports, fitness, streetwear, news headlines, hype reels, vertical social video.
options.vs: Extended is the opposite axis (wide). A condensed face is drawn narrow; horizontally scaling a regular font distorts stroke weights and looks amateur.
options.prompt: Set headlines in Anton or Barlow Condensed ExtraBold uppercase at 200-320px on 1080p, line-height 0.85, letter-spacing 0 to 0.01em, stacked 2-4 lines filling the frame height. Reveal each line with a vertical mask (yPercent 100 to 0) staggered 80ms, ease power4.out, 400ms.

options.what: A wide-width style with horizontally stretched proportions drawn into the design.
options.looks: Broad letters, horizontal emphasis, few words per line, space-age or luxury-tech feel. Google Fonts: Unbounded, Syncopate, Michroma, Krona One, Archivo at wdth 125. Commercial: Eurostile Extended, Druk Wide, Monument Extended, Microgramma.
options.motion: Tracking expansion, horizontal wipes, slow lateral drift, wide-to-regular width interpolation.
options.use: Automotive, tech hardware, crypto and Web3, fashion-tech, sci-fi titles.
options.vs: Condensed is the narrow axis. Wide letter-spacing on a normal face is tracking, not extended type.
options.prompt: Set short headlines in Unbounded or Michroma uppercase at 80-140px on 1080p, 1-3 words per line, letter-spacing 0.02em. Reveal with a horizontal wipe mask left to right over 600ms, ease power3.inOut, while tracking settles from 0.15em to 0.02em.

options.what: A sans with rounded stroke terminals and corners.
options.looks: Soft ends, friendly weight, often geometric bones. Google Fonts: Nunito, Quicksand, Fredoka, M PLUS Rounded 1c, Varela Round. Commercial: VAG Rounded, Arial Rounded, SF Pro Rounded.
options.motion: Squash-and-stretch pops, bouncy word-by-word entrances, wobble, playful counters.
options.use: Kids and family products, consumer apps, gaming, gentle onboarding, mascot-led brands.
options.vs: Inflated type is volumetric and puffy; rounded type only softens terminals. Geometric sans can have sharp terminals.
options.prompt: Set type in Fredoka or Nunito weight 600-800: headlines 110-150px on 1080p, letter-spacing 0, line-height 1.05. Pair with pill and circle shapes. Enter word-by-word: scale 0.6 to 1 with ease back.out(1.8), 350ms, stagger 70ms.

options.what: A single font file with continuous design axes (weight, width, optical size, slant or custom) that can be interpolated in motion.
options.looks: Depends on the face; the point is that weight, width or style can be any intermediate value. Google Fonts with rich axes: Roboto Flex, Fraunces (opsz, SOFT, WONK), Recursive (MONO, CASL), Anybody (wdth 50-150), Bricolage Grotesque (opsz, wdth). Commercial: GT Flexa, Whyte Inktrap Variable.
options.motion: Axis interpolation: weight breathing, width stretching, optical-size shifts, per-character wave through the weight axis.
options.use: Kinetic typography, music and audio-reactive visuals, brand stings, type-focused loops.
options.conveys: Fluidity, craft, technical sophistication; letters feel alive rather than animated as objects.
options.vs: Stretch/squash as a transform distorts glyph outlines; variable-font interpolation redraws the glyph correctly at each value. Choosing a variable font is a class choice; animating its axes is the motion facet.
options.prompt: Load a variable font with the axes you need (Roboto Flex for wght/wdth, Fraunces for wght/opsz/SOFT). Animate font-variation-settings directly on the GSAP timeline, e.g. from 'wght' 200 to 'wght' 900 over 800ms ease power2.inOut, per-character with stagger 30ms so a weight wave runs through the word.

options.what: Letters rendered as a stroke outline with a transparent or background-colored interior.
options.looks: Light, graphic, poster-like; usually a heavy display or condensed face so the outline reads. Google Fonts built-in: Bungee Outline, Monoton; any face via -webkit-text-stroke. Often alternated with filled lines.
options.motion: Outline-to-fill transitions, repeated outlined echoes behind a filled word, marquee scrolls, stroke draw-on.
options.use: Posters, fashion and streetwear, event promos, background type layers.
options.conveys: Lightness, style, rhythm; secondary emphasis next to filled type.
options.vs: Filled type is solid. Outline in iconography means a stroked icon; here it is only a text treatment.
options.prompt: Set a heavy face (Anton or Archivo Black) at 180px+ on 1080p with color transparent and -webkit-text-stroke 2-3px in the foreground color. Stack 3-5 outlined repeats of the word with one filled line; animate the filled line by tweening color from transparent to solid over 300ms.

options.what: Standard solid-color letterforms with no stroke, gradient or dimensional effect.
options.looks: Flat, maximum legibility, the default for all body text. Any typeface.
options.motion: Every standard reveal: masks, splits, color fills that sweep through the letters.
options.use: Nearly everything; named explicitly when contrasting with outlined or dimensional treatments.
options.vs: Outlined type is hollow; dimensional and extruded type add depth.
options.prompt: Render all type as flat solid fills in one or two palette colors: no strokes, gradients, shadows or glows. Emphasize with weight, size and a single accent color. Allow color-fill sweeps (a clip-path wipe of a second color over the word, 400ms) as the only treatment motion.

options.what: Flat type given apparent depth by offset layers, hard shadows or inline shading without true 3D geometry.
options.looks: Stacked offset copies, hard drop shadows, shaded bevels; retro sign-painting or sticker feel. Google Fonts: Bungee Shade, Bungee Inline, Rubik Mono One with layered text-shadow.
options.motion: Layers separating on entry, shadows sliding into place, parallax between stacked copies.
options.use: Retro and Y2K styling, playful social content, sticker-style brands, game promos.
options.vs: Extruded 3D type is true or faked volumetric depth with a continuous side surface; dimensional type is a 2D trick with discrete layers.
options.prompt: Set a heavy display face at 180px+ and build depth from 3-6 stacked copies offset 4px down-right each, alternating two palette colors (text-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #color1, 8px 8px 0 #color2). On entry, animate the offsets from 0 to full over 350ms, ease power3.out, so the layers peel apart.

options.what: Letterforms given continuous depth along the z-axis, with visible side walls, lit as objects.
options.looks: Solid 3D letters with bevels, side faces in a darker shade, lighting and perspective. In HTML: Three.js TextGeometry, or dense text-shadow stacks for a faked extrusion.
options.motion: 3D rotation revealing depth, extrusion growing from flat, camera orbits, letters tumbling in.
options.use: Title sequences, brand stings, gaming, event openers, maximalist social ads.
options.vs: Dimensional type stacks discrete flat layers; inflated type is puffy and rounded; chrome type is about surface reflection, not depth.
options.prompt: Render the headline as extruded 3D: depth 12-20% of cap height, 2-4px bevel, front face in the brand color and side walls 35% darker, key light top-left. Rotate from rotationY -35 to 0 over 900ms, ease power3.out, with the camera easing in 5%. In pure CSS fake it with 12-20 stacked 1px text-shadows.

options.what: Letterforms deliberately warped, sliced, displaced or glitched so the distortion becomes part of the message.
options.looks: Stretched, melted, sliced or RGB-split letters; mesh warps and displacement. Google Fonts: Rubik Glitch, Rubik Distressed; usually built with SVG filters (feTurbulence plus feDisplacementMap) or slice clones.
options.motion: Glitch bursts, slice offsets, displacement ramps, stretch-to-snap resolves.
options.use: Music, gaming, experimental brands, cybersecurity, fashion, glitch-aesthetic social content.
options.vs: Liquid type flows organically; distorted type breaks or warps sharply. Scramble/decode changes characters; distortion changes shapes.
options.prompt: Distort the headline in bursts, not constantly: 3-5 horizontal slice clones offset 10-40px for 2-3 frames, a 3px RGB split, then snap back clean. Or apply an SVG feDisplacementMap whose scale ramps 0 to 40 to 0 over 500ms. Keep the resolved state perfectly legible for at least 1s.

options.what: Type that appears to flow, drip, ripple or melt like a liquid.
options.looks: Gooey joins, drips, ripple distortions, glossy blobs; often a gooey SVG filter (blur plus alpha threshold). Google Fonts: Rubik Puddles, Rubik Wet Paint for static versions.
options.motion: Letters merging and separating, ripple waves, drip-down exits, metaball morphs.
options.use: Beverage, beauty, music visuals, experimental brand content, Y2K revival.
options.vs: Distorted type breaks sharply; inflated type is puffy but solid. 'Liquid type' is an informal studio term.
options.prompt: Apply a gooey filter to the headline: SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 8 then feColorMatrix alpha threshold (values 0 0 0 18 -7). Animate letters drifting 10-30px apart and back so they merge, or ripple a feDisplacementMap turbulence baseFrequency 0.01-0.02 over 2s. Use a glossy highlight for wet feel.

options.what: Letterforms rendered with a reflective polished-metal surface.
options.looks: Banded horizon reflections, hard highlight lines, dark-to-bright gradients; usually heavy, wide or blackletter display faces. In HTML: multi-stop linear-gradient clipped to text, or environment-mapped Three.js.
options.motion: Specular highlight sweeps, slow rotation catching light, glints on arrival.
options.use: Y2K and rave revival, music, streetwear, gaming, premium tech teasers.
options.conveys: Hype, futurism, luxury, nostalgia for late-90s/2000s graphics.
options.vs: Extruded type is about depth; chrome is about surface. Gradient type without banded reflections is not chrome.
options.prompt: Render the headline with background-clip:text and a chrome gradient: linear-gradient(180deg, #f5f7fa 0%, #9aa3ad 45%, #2a2f36 50%, #cfd6de 60%, #ffffff 100%), plus a 1px light top edge. Sweep a narrow white highlight band across it (background-position 0% to 200%) over 1.2s once per shot.

options.what: Letterforms rendered as soft, pressurized volumes, like balloons or pillows.
options.looks: Rounded swollen shapes, soft highlights, subtle ambient occlusion where letters touch. Google Fonts: Rubik Bubbles, Bagel Fat One, Titan One, Chango (flat versions); true inflation is 3D.
options.motion: Inflate from flat, squash-and-stretch bounces, jiggle on impact, deflate exits.
options.use: Consumer apps, kids, candy and snack brands, playful 3D social content.
options.vs: Rounded type only softens terminals; extruded type has flat faces and hard walls; inflated has no flat faces.
options.prompt: Render the word in Bagel Fat One or Titan One with an inflated look: radial highlight top-left, soft inner shadow on the lower edge, and a soft contact shadow. Enter with scale 0 to 1.12 to 0.96 to 1 over 600ms (ease elastic.out(1, 0.5)) with scaleY lagging scaleX by 60ms for squash and stretch.

options.what: Letterforms built on a coarse pixel grid, imitating bitmap screen fonts.
options.looks: Stair-stepped edges, square dots, no anti-aliasing. Google Fonts: Silkscreen, Press Start 2P, VT323, Pixelify Sans, Tiny5.
options.motion: Stepped (non-eased) motion, character-by-character appearance, blinking, frame-rate-limited movement.
options.use: Gaming, retro-tech, developer culture, playful dashboards, 8-bit nostalgia.
options.vs: Monospace is fixed width but smooth; pixel type is built from a bitmap grid and must be scaled in integer multiples.
options.prompt: Set text in Silkscreen or Press Start 2P at integer multiples of its grid (e.g. 32, 48, 64px), with -webkit-font-smoothing none and image-rendering pixelated on any rasters. Animate with steps() easing (ease 'steps(8)') so movement snaps on a grid; reveal character-by-character at 40ms.

options.what: Type scaled beyond the frame so letters become shapes.
options.prompt: Set the key word so it fills 90-120% of frame width at 300-500px on 1080p, allowed to crop at the edges; everything else under 28px. Move it slowly (x drift 3-5% over 3s) so the crop reveals different letters.

options.what: Deliberately small type set against large empty space or imagery.
options.prompt: Set text at 18-24px on 1080p, uppercase tracked 0.08-0.12em or small sentence case, placed in corners or along a margin, with 70%+ of the frame empty. Use it as labels and captions next to one large image.

options.what: Type centered on both axes as the single focus.
options.prompt: Center one line (max 7 words) horizontally and optically (1-3% above true center), nothing else on screen. Reveal and exit symmetrically from the middle outward.

options.what: Magazine-style layout with off-center blocks, hanging text and deliberate tension.
options.prompt: Place the headline flush-left on columns 1-7 of a 12-column grid, a small caption on columns 9-12 aligned to the headline baseline, and a large blank area. Mix serif display and small sans labels.

options.what: Every text block snaps to a visible or implied column and baseline grid.
options.prompt: Use a 12-column grid with 80px margins and 24px gutters and an 8px baseline grid on 1920x1080; every text block starts on a column edge and moves by whole columns when repositioned.

options.what: Words stacked in tight lines so the block reads as a shape.
options.prompt: Stack 3-5 short words, one per line, line-height 0.85-0.9, same width or justified by size so the block forms a rectangle; reveal line by line with 80ms stagger.

options.what: Text rotated 90 degrees or set in vertical columns.
options.prompt: Rotate secondary labels 90 degrees (writing-mode: vertical-rl or rotate -90) along the left or right edge at 20-28px, tracked 0.1em, as a rail; slide it along its axis on entry.

options.what: Type carries the visual role of a picture: textured, filled with footage or used as a shape.
options.prompt: Make the word the main image: fill it with footage or a gradient via background-clip:text or an SVG mask, at 300px+ with heavy weight, and let the fill move while the letters hold.

options.what: Screens packed with text blocks, labels and data, reading as texture.
options.prompt: Fill the frame with 6-12 text blocks at 3-4 sizes on a strict grid, small leading, labels and numbers in monospace; animate blocks in quick cascades (stagger 30-40ms).

options.what: Minimal words with large amounts of empty space.
options.prompt: Show no more than one line (3-6 words) per screen, 75%+ negative space, holds of 1.5-2.5s; transitions are slow and single-element.

options.what: Characters appear one at a time with a cursor, as if typed.
options.prompt: Reveal characters sequentially at 35-55ms each (vary +-15ms for human feel), no easing, with a block or bar cursor blinking every 530ms that tracks the last character; pause 250ms at punctuation.

options.what: Each glyph animates individually with a stagger.
options.prompt: SplitText by chars; each char yPercent 100 to 0 inside a line mask (or opacity 0 to 1 plus y 20px), 400ms, ease power3.out, stagger 20-30ms.

options.what: Each word enters as a unit, staggered.
options.prompt: SplitText by words; each word y 40px to 0 and opacity 0 to 1, 450ms, ease power3.out, stagger 60-90ms; time the stagger to the voiceover if there is one.

options.what: Each line of a paragraph or headline enters as a unit.
options.prompt: SplitText by lines with each line wrapped in an overflow-hidden mask; lines yPercent 105 to 0, 700ms, ease power4.out, stagger 100-120ms.

options.what: Text slides into view from behind an invisible edge.
options.prompt: Wrap each line in overflow:hidden; slide text from yPercent 100 (bottom-up) to 0 over 600-800ms, ease power3.out or expo.out. Exit the same way upward. No opacity change.

options.what: A moving edge uncovers static text.
options.prompt: Animate clip-path from inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) left-to-right over 500-700ms, ease power2.inOut; optionally lead with a solid color bar that wipes on then off.

options.what: A word hits the screen oversized and settles, often on a beat.
options.prompt: Word scale 1.4 to 1.0 in 180-250ms, ease power4.out, landing exactly on the beat; optional 2-frame 4px shake. Hard cut to the next word.

options.what: Letter-spacing opens up over time.
options.prompt: Tween letter-spacing from -0.02em to 0.3em over 1.5-3s, ease power1.out, with opacity rising in the first 30%; center-aligned so it grows symmetrically.

options.what: Widely spaced letters collapse into a tight word.
options.prompt: Tween letter-spacing from 0.5em to -0.03em over 700ms, ease expo.out, center-aligned, landing on a beat.

options.what: Words rearrange, resize and reflow between compositions.
options.prompt: Use GSAP Flip: record word positions, change the layout (size, line breaks, alignment), then Flip.from over 700ms ease power3.inOut so each word travels to its new place.

options.what: One word in a fixed sentence swaps through alternatives.
options.prompt: Keep the sentence static; the swapped word rolls vertically inside a mask (out yPercent -100, in from 100) every 600-900ms, 300ms, ease power3.inOut; the container width tweens to fit each word.

options.what: One word transforms into another through shared letters.
options.prompt: Use Flip to move letters shared by both words to their new positions; fade and scale out unshared letters and bring new ones in, all over 800ms ease power2.inOut.

options.what: Glyph outlines morph into other glyphs or shapes.
options.prompt: Convert glyphs to SVG paths and tween between them with MorphSVGPlugin over 500-700ms, ease power2.inOut; prefer round-to-round glyph pairs so the in-betweens stay clean.

options.what: A variable font's axes animate continuously.
options.prompt: Tween font-variation-settings (e.g. 'wght' 100 to 900, 'wdth' 75 to 125) over 600-1200ms ease sine.inOut, per char with 30-40ms stagger so the change travels through the word as a wave.

options.what: Type elongates along one axis for speed or emphasis.
options.prompt: Scale Y 1 to 1.6 (or X via the wdth axis) over 250ms as the word moves, then settle to 1 with ease power3.out; set transform-origin at the baseline.

options.what: Type compresses on impact.
options.prompt: On landing, scaleY 0.75 and scaleX 1.15 for 80ms, then back to 1 over 200ms ease back.out(2), transform-origin bottom center.

options.what: Letters or words rotate in 2D.
options.prompt: Each char rotation from -90 to 0 with transform-origin bottom left, 500ms, ease back.out(1.4), stagger 25ms; or a whole word rotating 90 degrees to swap with the next.

options.what: Characters oscillate in a traveling sine wave.
options.prompt: SplitText by chars; y from 0 to -18px, 400ms, ease sine.inOut, yoyo, repeat as needed, stagger each 0.06s so a wave travels left to right.

options.what: Type drops or pops in with a physical bounce.
options.prompt: Each word from y -120px to 0 over 700ms ease bounce.out (or back.out(2) for a single overshoot), stagger 80ms; avoid for serious or premium tones.

options.what: Letters or words rearrange position before settling in order.
options.prompt: Start chars in randomized positions within the word's bounding box and tween to their correct x over 600ms ease power3.inOut with random stagger (stagger { each: 0.02, from: 'random' }).

options.what: Random characters cycle before resolving to the real text.
options.prompt: Use ScrambleTextPlugin: text resolves over 800-1200ms with chars 'upperCase' or '01', revealDelay 0.2, speed 0.4; best in monospace so width holds steady.

options.what: Text runs along a curve or shape.
options.prompt: Place text on an SVG textPath (circle or bezier); animate startOffset from 100% to 0% over 2-4s ease none for a traveling line, or rotate a circular path 360 degrees slowly.

options.what: Digits roll vertically like an odometer.
options.prompt: Build each digit as a vertical strip 0-9 inside a one-digit-tall mask; tween each strip's yPercent to its target over 900-1400ms ease power3.out, rightmost digit spinning farther. Tabular figures only.

options.what: A number counts up or down to its value.
options.prompt: Tween a proxy {v:0} to the target over 1-1.8s ease power2.out, writing Math.round(v) with locale separators into the element on update; tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) so width stays fixed.

options.what: Type grows depth from flat to 3D.
options.prompt: Grow extrusion depth from 0 to full over 600ms ease power3.out (Three.js scale.z, or add text-shadow layers progressively), while rotating 15-25 degrees on Y to show the side walls.

options.what: Letters or lines flip in perspective.
options.prompt: Parent perspective 800px; each line rotationX from -90 to 0 with transformOrigin '50% 50% -40px', 700ms, ease power3.out, stagger 80ms (a flap-board flip).

options.what: A word grows to fill the frame and becomes the cut to the next scene.
options.prompt: Scale one heavy word from 1 to 40+ over 700ms ease expo.in, aiming the zoom into a counter or stroke so its fill covers the frame; cut to the next scene on the frame of full coverage.

options.what: Letterforms act as windows onto footage or another scene.
options.prompt: Use the headline as an SVG mask or background-clip:text over footage; hold the image moving inside the letters, then scale the mask up until the image fills the frame.

options.what: Type properties respond to the soundtrack's amplitude or beats.
options.prompt: Pre-analyze the audio into per-frame amplitude and beat times; drive scale (1 to 1.08), weight axis or letter-spacing from amplitude on the timeline, with punches on detected beats. No live analysis at render time.
